entries.original: A `thread_send` to a busy thread on another device that was queued there as a follow-up now answers `queued` with its `delivery_id` and `effective_mode`. It used to answer `idempotency_uncertain` ("accepted the message but did not report where it waits") even though the message was delivered and answered. The receiving engine's `queued` admission is its receipt, and its pending-message count does not include admitted deliveries. entries.original: A reply to a peer on another device no longer answers `not_found` when the delivery that brought the peer's message carries no device attestation (an `rpc:local/<id>` or bare delivery id). If this device holds no session by that id or stated name, the reply is looked up account-wide. It is delivered only to the session the sender's durable id names; another match is `reply_target_mismatch`, and an id that more than one device lists is `ambiguous_target` with nothing sent. entries.original: `thread_list` no longer reports the sessions of a device that is offline or did not answer as live. Their rows come from the relay's cached snapshot and are now listed `resumable`; opening one with `thread_create` asks that device to reopen it, and answers `device_offline` while the device stays offline. entries.original: `thread_read` and the thread control tools no longer answer `not_found` for a session that another device of the account holds but runs nowhere, when it is addressed by session id. `thread_read`, `thread_interrupt`, `thread_rename`, `thread_set_model` and `thread_set_reasoning` answer `not_resumable`, and `thread_close` answers `closed: false` with reason `not_live`, as on the device that holds it. entries.original: `thread_create` on this device no longer leaves a prompt-less thread when the connection closes after the host made the session. The create finds the thread it made and answers it, and a retry under the same `idempotency_key` answers the same thread and admits the prompt exactly once. A retry that cannot find that thread here (a create on another device, or a host that ignored the derived id) still answers `idempotency_uncertain`. ([#14066](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14066))

entries.original: Cold wake: the OmO session host service no longer restarts itself every 30 seconds on Linux and macOS. entries.original: `omo account store enable` keeps the sign-in in OmO's own keychain on a Mac whose login keychain stays locked, for example when another macOS user holds the screen or omo runs over SSH. The store is opt-in. `disable` moves the sign-in back, and `status` reports which store is in use. omo never changes the keychain search list or the default keychain, and never falls back between stores. ([#14033](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/14033))

entries.original: **Thread tools:** `thread_create` survives a lost open reply and retries exactly once (#14060, #14066). It names a device by display name, id or unique id prefix (#14072).
